The run reached its API budget limit; some analysis or evidence verification could not finish.

CORE RESEARCH

AMD / Non current assets

Explore evidence ↓
4 earnings calls · 8 SEC filings · 8 issuer documents8 reporting periods · 173 evidence entries

Earnings-call coverage: 4/8 reporting periods. No call was searched for Q1 2023, Q2 2023, Q3 2023, Q1 2024.

THE ANSWER

What the sources show

Across 2023 and into 2024, the disclosed drivers of working-capital movements that relate to non-current asset support (e.g., inventory ramp and technology-license prepayments) appear repeatedly in the cash-flow discussion of operating assets. In early 2023, changes in operating assets referenced increases in accounts receivable and prepaid expenses/other assets driven by prepayments under long-term supply agreements. Through 2022-2023 and into 2024, the company repeatedly attributes inventory increases to ramping Data Center and Client products in advanced process nodes, with additional inventory build described in 2024 as anticipation of those ramps. The inventory and prepaid expenses pattern suggests ongoing investment and longer-cycle supply/technology arrangements that would be consistent with growth in non-current asset categories, though the excerpts provided do not quantify specific non-current asset balances. In the later 2024 disclosures, the company also introduces tax-valuation-allowance language for deferred tax assets (a non-current asset component), emphasizing that valuation allowances depend on whether recovery is more-likely-than-not.

Watch points

  • The provided excerpts discuss “Long-Lived and Intangible Assets” and include deferred tax asset valuation-allowance accounting guidance, but do not include the actual non-current asset line-item balances or detailed rollforwards, limiting comparability across periods.
  • The inventory-ramp narrative is repeated, yet the excerpt set does not explain potential impairment, useful-life changes, or asset recovery considerations—important for non-current asset risk assessment.
  • Deferred tax assets: the disclosure specifies a more-likely-than-not (probability level of more than 50%) threshold for recovery; lack of period-specific valuation allowance changes in the excerpts makes the evolution of this non-current asset risk unclear.
  • Long-cycle investment/ramp support reflected in recurring inventory and prepaid expense increases
  • Timing risk in working-capital items (accounts receivable, inventory receipts, accounts payable payments)
  • Deferred tax assets subject to valuation-allowance recoverability assessment

  • jump to section"The primary drivers of the change in operating assets and liabilities were a $1.9 billion increase in accounts receivable due to the timing of customer payments and higher revenue, a $1.1 billion increase in inventory primarily to support the continued ramp of Data Center products in advanced process technology nodes and $1.0 billion of tax payments."
  • jump to section"The forward-looking statements relate to, among other things: possible impact of future accounting rules on AMD’s condensed consolidated financial statements; demand for AMD’s products; the expectation that AMD’s cash, cash equivalents and short-term investment balances, together with the availability under that certain revolving credit facility made available to AMD and certain of its subsidiaries, our commercial paper program, and our cash flows from operations will be sufficient to fund AMD’s operations including capital expenditures, purchase commitments and acquisitions over the next 12 months and beyond; AMD’s ability to access capital markets; AMD’s ability to obtain sufficient external financing on favorable terms, or at all; AMD’s expectation that based on management’s current knowledge, the potential liability related to AMD’s current litigation will not have a material adverse effect on its financial positions, results of operation or cash flows; anticipated ongoing and increased costs related to enhancing and implementing information security controls; AMD’s expectation that all unbilled accounts receivables are expected to be billed and collected within 12 months; that revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations that are unsatisfied which will be recognized in the next 12 months and that a small number of customers will continue to account for a substantial part of AMD’s revenue in the future; the expected implications from the development of the legal and regulatory environment relating to emerging technologies, such as AI; AMD’s ability to achieve its corporate responsibility initiatives; expected future AI trends and developments; the expected benefits of AMD’s acquisition of Silo AI Oy (Silo AI); AMD’s anticipated acquisition of ZT Group Int’l, Inc.
